correctness.rationale: The irreducible Φ_(p²) gives a necessary and sufficient vanishing criterion for each p²-root sum. The mask has three cases, including the crucial proof that one nonzero monomial in each residue class cannot sum to zero. Orthogonality forces p equally sized residue blocks each with distinct U+V values; this proves both directions of the unique basis parametrization and count. All affine cyclic cosets are enumerated separately. Exact cyclotomic checks on primes 2,3,5,7 corroborate without replacing the uniform proof.

value.rationale: The entire family of p^p residue-digit graphs, including the Frobenius graph, has a common Fourier-zero geometry and p^(p²+p) exactly parameterized orthogonal bases. Knowing a graph tiles implies none of this census; the affine count p⁴−p³ and concrete nonlinear bases reveal nontrivial combinatorial structure of admissible Fourier reconstructions. These exact natural invariants are motivated by Fourier spectral pairs on nonfield prime-power groups.
